We take our resident dog, Chibi, here for checkups.
We don't trust other hospitals, but this doctor is very experienced and we truly believe in him.
It's busy, but they prioritize emergencies.

The dog came back very dirty and black, and had a large mat of fur behind its ear.
It looked like someone had forcibly removed it, as there was a patch of hairless skin and it was red. When I inquired, they didn't do anything to help. Don't go there. I don't even want to give them one star.

It's been over eight years since we started having our two Chihuahua-Poodle mix twins, a boy and a girl, examined by you when they were three months old. Now we have three more, and you take care of the grooming and physical examinations of our five adorable puppies. You truly love animals, and I'm always worried about your health because I never know when you're resting. I'm 65 myself, so I wonder how many more years I'll be able to be with my puppies. Please take care of your health, Doctor, and continue to be their doctor for a long time to come. Fight on, Doctor!

My beloved dog recently passed away while being groomed here.
It was so sudden that not only my children but I also cried and mourned immensely. I'm still in the midst of grief.

This is a long story, but I would like anyone considering coming here to read it carefully before making a decision. However, for those of you who are busy, I'll summarize the main points:

- There was absolutely no apology for my dog's death.
- The director, hospital staff, and groomers all took care of my dog ​​without knowing his age or medical history.
- When I asked what had happened to his previous medical records, I was told that anything older than five years had been disposed of. (If you didn't hear anything like that, let me write it again.)
- The director, because the accident occurred on his day off, said, "I actually have something I want to do today, so please hurry up with the time to collect the body."
- When I expressed regret that my body had returned as a dead body, the director became angry.
- The groomer, who claimed to have over 20 years of experience, remained silent throughout.

Details below.

I first came here for a grooming session a few years ago, and I think I wrote something like a simple medical record.
*I usually go to a different hospital, and only came here for grooming.

I hadn't been there in a while, but I couldn't get an appointment at my usual salon, so I brought my dog ​​here.

I thought they were calling it a medical record and providing the treatment.

A few days before the grooming session
I personally went to the salon to make the appointment (they asked for my name and contact information, so I assumed they were using it as a medical record).

The day
■11:30 AM: My family takes my dog ​​to the salon in a carrier.
・They tell me we'll finish around 1:30 PM and to come pick him up.
・They call me and ask about the length of the haircut.

(I'm sure there were other questions they needed to ask...)

■Around 1:00 PM: The family who had left my dog ​​with me receives a call informing them that my dog ​​had collapsed and died during the treatment.
・According to the family, it was the director, but there was no apology whatsoever. They just explained the situation and told me they were off duty and to come and retrieve the body quickly...

・I immediately called myself and, panicked, asked for more details.
・My dog ​​was fine until the hairdryer, but collapsed during the treatment and they tried to resuscitate him, but he died. It appears he had pulmonary edema, so it's possible he had been ill for some time. (So ​​they pretended not to take responsibility.)
- They understood the situation, said they would go and retrieve the body, and then hung up the phone.

■Around 2:00 PM
- Arrived at the hospital. The director handled the call alone. With the body in front of them, they received almost the same explanation as they had received over the phone.
- When I asked to call the groomer, a middle-aged female groomer reluctantly appeared from the back. She didn't even greet me.
- The director asked the groomer, "What do you think about this? You haven't apologized a word since the phone call."
- The director replied, "I'm sorry for your loss, but we did resuscitate him, so there's nothing to apologize for." The groomer remained silent.
- It's true that another veterinarian had told me that his heart was slightly damaged, and he had regular checkups. Neither I nor my family were ever asked about this, but when I asked what had happened to his medical records, they said they had looked for them after he died but couldn't find any.
- Shocked, she replied, "Huh? "So, did you take in and groom my dog ​​without knowing his medical history, let alone how old he was?" I asked, and he replied, "Yes."

Isn't that a problem? I asked, and he mumbled, "We process the medical records five years after the last visit." I was confused at the time and didn't say much, but if you think about it, the lack of a medical record should have been obvious before the dog was taken in, and if that's the case, they should have made the dog fill it out again. Incidentally, the director even offered a light apology, saying, "I'm sorry about that."

The issues gradually narrowed down to "I took my dog ​​in without disclosing his medical history in advance" and "They didn't ask about his medical history, and there were no medical records." Since emotional arguments wouldn't get us anywhere, he left the hospital with the body, saying he'd contact me through his lawyer.

There was no apology until the very end.

We're currently preparing for trial.

That's roughly what happened.

Here are my thoughts now, a week after this incident.

The point is, he didn't mean to apologize because it would be detrimental in a lawsuit if he made such a remark.

I hate to say this, but the doctor was a very elderly man (I think he was over 80), and it seemed like the type of person who would apologize was completely out of his league (I'd never imagined it like that before...).

That made me feel very uncomfortable.

By the way, the groomer had been working at a pet salon for about 20 years, but the cut was poorly done.

I asked the groomer, "It's true that he had a slightly impaired heart, so I understand that this kind of thing happens, but won't you apologize for the fact that the dog ultimately died?" But, for better or worse, unlike a doctor, he just remained silent. (It didn't seem like it was a hospital order, either.)

Apparently, they dispose of medical records for patients who haven't visited the salon within the last five years. I'd never heard of such a thing, so I wondered if they were going to let the patient get groomed without any patient data. When I asked about this, the director, as expected, apologized. I'm not sure if it had been more than five years since her last visit, but I still feel very distrustful that we accepted her without any data or medical history.

For that reason, I feel very disappointed to just brush it off as an accident during grooming, and I still haven't been able to process it myself.

As with human hospitals, I have great respect for those who work in jobs that involve lives, such as veterinary clinics, grooming salons, and babysitting services. Therefore, I always try to avoid making unreasonable remarks that make it difficult for such people to do their jobs. However, in this case, if they had asked about her medical history when she was booked for grooming, or at least asked about her age, and if they had realized in advance that she died after being treated without any medical records, I can't help but think about so many things and it's painful.

Also, if both the director and the sitter had sincerely apologized at the time of the accident, without worrying too much about what would happen next...even if it wasn't that extreme, just a simple apology...it would have made me feel so much better. In fact, when I had my cat's ear trimmed at another place before, they sincerely apologized, and I felt like I was taking the risk into consideration when leaving my cat there. I accepted the apology and continued using their services.

I never imagined that my cat would come back in this condition, even though there was a veterinary clinic attached to the salon, and I now regret being so naive.

Thank you for reading this far.

I hope you will be aware that there are untrustworthy grooming salons out there, not just this one, even if they have a veterinary clinic attached.

(11-year-old Chihuahua)

The prices are reasonable, but it's at the level of a local doctor's office. It's fine for minor things like colds or vaccinations. It's not at the level of a university hospital or general hospital. The medical equipment is old and therefore not very accurate. My child was given unnecessary medication and medication that didn't suit his symptoms for a long period of time, and they gave up on us, saying there was nothing more they could do. They spoke as if we were just waiting for him to die, so we went to another hospital. There, they told us to stop the medication he was currently taking immediately, and as a result, they saved his life. If we had listened to Dr. Endo... I truly believe we didn't give up. So, I recommend getting a second opinion for long-term treatment. I will never go back there again to protect my child.

It's clear the doctor loves animals.

My dog ​​enjoys the visit and behaves well during the examination. I feel at ease thanks to the doctor's extensive knowledge and thorough explanations.

My cat was in pain in her mouth, so I took her in.

I was worried that even just a teeth cleaning would be very expensive, but the vet said, "I can get this out quickly," and removed the tartar in an instant.

Her technique was amazing.

Her canine gums were also swollen, but after examining the condition of her teeth and gums, the vet didn't force an extraction and instead gave her oral medication.

The billing was transparent, and the details were easier to understand than a human medical bill. (I think it's significantly cheaper than the going rate.)

The vet has a gentle tone, which is also reassuring.

My cat, who hated having her mouth touched even a little, seemed perfectly fine after we got home.

Veteran Dr. Endo is amazing!

The doctor is hardworking, experienced, and I can talk to them about anything; I trust them completely.

It's very crowded.

It's best not to leave your rabbit here. As others have mentioned, it lives on newspaper (its paws were black). When I brought it to the vet, the carrier was overflowing with urine, and you could tell by the smell without even looking inside. Sure enough, when I took it out of the carrier, it was completely covered in urine.
If you can't take care of it properly, please remove the listing as a pet hotel for small animals. If you're taking money, I expect the service to match.
I've been a customer for over 16 years.
They make me wait in the store for at least an hour every single time I come for reservation.

I recently left my rabbit at a veterinary clinic for three nights and four days. However, the clinic disregarded the feeding instructions I initially gave, giving my rabbit excessive amounts of rabbit food. When the extra food I brought ran out, they fed it some unknown food from the clinic. As a result, my rabbit's grass consumption drastically decreased.

They didn't contact me at all before giving the rabbit the clinic's food; it was done without my permission. They didn't even tell me what kind of food they were giving it.

My rabbit came back completely black with ink, apparently having lived on newspaper.

When I informed the head veterinarian of the above, he treated it as a complaint and responded with a condescending attitude, telling me not to come back. Perhaps he was upset that his pride had been hurt, but he showed absolutely no empathy for the animal. I felt he lacked a sense of responsibility for looking after someone else's family member.

I have decided I would never entrust my precious family member to a clinic again.

Fortunately, my rabbit is not showing any health problems, but I hope that no one else suffers the same fate.

Dr. Endo saved the lives of the dog and cat I had as a child, as well as my two current cats. They're now 17 and 7 years old. When my 7-year-old was 3 years old, I noticed a lump under his left jaw and immediately examined him. He examined him with an ultrasound and, noting something unpleasant, immediately referred him to the Japan Advanced Medical Center. The next day, he was diagnosed with lymphoma. We immediately decided to start chemotherapy, which put him in remission. With lymphoma, there's no time to worry! The decision is up to the owner. In my case, my cat only had three months to live, so the prompt chemotherapy was extremely effective. I truly have nothing but gratitude for Dr. Endo. Dr. Endo and the female nurses (?) are not very talkative, but their kindness is palpable. Thank you as always.
Our family has decided to use this clinic again. We used to go to a different animal hospital because it's a bit far, but this is definitely the most reliable and excellent vet we can trust.
